findings.title: ANY() on JS arrays will fail when team/org SQL runs
findings.body: Org and team authorization bind id lists as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` (line 164), `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (line 168), and `"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` (line 201). Prisma's raw-query engine does not send a JavaScript number array as a PostgreSQL array parameter; it is passed as text such as `[1,2,3]`. PostgreSQL then rejects the statement (`malformed array literal` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`) instead of returning bookings. Team and org insights therefore error at runtime. Use scalar binding, for example `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or `= ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[])`, and keep the existing empty-list guard because `Prisma.join([])` throws. The new `$queryRaw` test only executes the user-scope predicate (`"userId" = $1 AND "teamId" IS NULL`), which never uses `ANY`, so this failure is not covered.

findings.title: toEqual(Prisma.sql) does not match composed fragments
findings.body: Team-scope (line 295), org-scope (line 332), and combined-filter (line 429) expectations are a single flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service builds those predicates with `reduce` into `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})`, which stores nested `Prisma.Sql` objects in `.values` and only flattens them when the query is executed. Vitest `toEqual` compares `.strings` and `.values` and does not render nested fragments, so these three assertions fail even when the SQL that would be sent is equivalent. User-scope and single-filter tests pass only because those paths return one flat template. Assert a flattened rendering, or build the expected value with the same nesting, otherwise CI cannot validate the composed authorization SQL.

findings.title: Team scope without teamId now typechecks and returns no rows
findings.body: The constructor previously required `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, the zod discriminated union that makes `teamId` mandatory when `scope` is `"team"`. It now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. A team-scoped call that omits `teamId` still fails `safeParse`, is stored as `this.options = null`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns `1=0` with no error. Callers get an empty insights result that looks like "no bookings" instead of a compile-time or thrown validation error. Keep the discriminated union on the constructor, or throw when `safeParse` fails, so a missing `teamId` cannot be confused with an authorized empty set.
